subject.title: [Bug]: 2026.6.x regression cascade — memory search broken, then sessions lost on every reconnect (multi-agent deployment broken)

question: Should this umbrella remain the coordinating P1 for the 2026.6.x regression cascade, or should maintainers split the remaining work now that the QMD zero-hit slice has landed on main?
rationale: The issue mixes fixed current-main memory work, unresolved session identity behavior, open memory provider-routing work, crash/config proof gaps, and proposed new config/UI surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent tracking shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split focused blockers
options.body: Keep this issue open as the coordinating report while maintainers link or create narrower session reconnect, memory routing, and crash/config follow-ups and close it only after those are resolved or rejected.

options.title: Convert to narrower canonical issues
options.body: Move the remaining slices into separate canonical issues and leave this issue only as historical context once each remaining failure has a clear owner.

options.title: Treat the migration hypothesis as unproven
options.body: Reject the single-root-cause framing and triage the surviving symptoms independently based on fresh live proof.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split focused blockers
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the coordinating report while maintainers link or create narrower session reconnect, memory routing, and crash/config follow-ups and close it only after those are resolved or rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent maintainer-facing review context on the QMD fix and adjacent QMD ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the split-or-keep decision.
